topic: A duplicate order from a double tap or a retry after a timeout — why disabling the button is not enough, and how an idempotency key from the app plus a unique index in Azure SQL guarantees one order and one charge.

title.sub: A double tap charges the customer twice.

stages.title: One tap, two orders
stages.desc: A double tap sends the same order twice, to two different servers.
stages.narration: A double tap on Place order. Two requests, two servers, two orders.

stages.title: Or a slow network
stages.desc: The order succeeds at 10.4 s. The app gave up at 10 s and says "try again".
stages.status: timeout 10 s · server finished at 10.4 s
stages.narration: Or the network is slow. The app times out, and the customer taps again.

stages.title: The server can't tell
stages.desc: Same user, same cart, same total. Nothing says the two requests are one order.
stages.narration: The server cannot tell a retry from a new order. Identical.

stages.title: Disable the button?
stages.desc: It stops a double tap. A retry after a timeout still gets through.
stages.narration: Disabling the button stops a double tap. It does not stop a retry.

stages.title: One key per order
stages.desc: The app creates a random key when checkout starts. Every retry reuses it.
stages.narration: Fix it in the app. One key per order, reused on retry.

stages.title: The database decides
stages.desc: A unique index on (UserId, IdempotencyKey). The second insert fails with 2601.
stages.narration: A unique index in Azure SQL. The second insert with that key fails.

stages.title: Return the same order
stages.desc: The repeat gets the original order back. Nothing is inserted twice.
stages.narration: The repeat gets the original order back. Nothing new is created.

stages.title: Charge once
stages.desc: The payment gateway gets the same key, so even a resent charge counts once.
stages.narration: Send the same key to the payment gateway. One charge.

stages.title: The next Friday
stages.desc: Slow gateway again. 311 retries, all answered with the saved order.
stages.narration: Next slow Friday: hundreds of retries, and zero duplicate orders.

stages.title: Let the database decide
stages.desc: A key from the app. A unique index in Azure SQL. One order per tap.
stages.narration: One tap, one order. Let the database decide.

end.title: One tap. One order. Let the database decide.
end.sub: Send an idempotency key from the app, and enforce it with a unique index in Azure SQL.

post.caption:
Picture a Friday dinner rush where nothing is down, and 214 customers are charged twice. 🍛

Two causes, found with one SQL query:
1. Double taps, under a second apart.
2. Retries after a 10-second timeout, where the first order had already worked.

THE REAL PROBLEM
The server could not tell a retry from a new order. Same user, same cart, same total. Only the id was different.

WHY DISABLING THE BUTTON IS NOT ENOUGH
It stops a second tap on one screen. It does nothing for a retry, a second tab, an old app version or a request the network resends.

THE FIX: AN IDEMPOTENCY KEY
1. The app creates a random key when the order starts, and reuses it on every retry.
2. The API requires it: Idempotency-Key header.
3. Azure SQL enforces it:

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX UX_Orders_User_IdempotencyKey
  ON dbo.Orders (UserId, IdempotencyKey)
  WHERE IdempotencyKey IS NOT NULL;

4. A repeat fails with error 2601. The API returns the order it already made.
5. The payment gateway gets the same key, so the card is charged once.

One tap, one order, one charge. On any server, at any timing.

Full incident write-up: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/duplicate-order-idempotency-key-azure-sql
